1. [b-falling-dust] A sparse descending fan of tiny angular grains within faint gas, aligned toward the young disk plane. IMPORTANT: Representative enlarged grains, not a shower of planet-sized boulders.
2. [b-slow-grains] Separated small angular dry grains with gently converging spacing and several near contacts. IMPORTANT: Slow relative motion cannot be proven by a still image; distinguish spatial pattern and preserve name.
3. [b-fast-grains] A narrow oblique train of the same small angular grains crossing empty space. IMPORTANT: No flame or velocity token; motion direction is contextual and must survive without invented arrows.
4. [b-settled-dust] A thin broad horizontal band of fine grains with a denser central plane and diffuse grains above it. IMPORTANT: A settled reservoir, not a single clump or a completed rocky body.
5. [b-fluffy-clumps] Two or three open lacy aggregates of angular grains with large internal voids. IMPORTANT: Keep visible porosity; not compact stone pebbles.
6. [b-chipped-grains] Dispersed angular fragments with remnants of the former lacy aggregate at one side. IMPORTANT: Destructive fragmentation, not evaporation, smoke or returned identical intact clump.
7. [b-rebuilt-clumps] New lacy aggregates containing angular chips and finer adherent dust, an arrangement unlike the original clumps. IMPORTANT: Same material lineage, not resurrection of the original unique shape.
8. [b-hard-pebbles] Three compact irregular rounded pebbles with closed, solid surfaces. IMPORTANT: Denser than porous clumps; not full spherical worlds.
9. [b-icy-grains] Irregular rock grains with visibly pale rounded frost mantles, a few in an inward-curving chain. IMPORTANT: Ice is a coating on grains, not blue gemstones or droplets.
10. [b-ground-icy-grains] Smaller broken angular grain cores with patchy retained pale frost around their edges. IMPORTANT: Retain visible ice unlike b-dry-grains; fragmentation has not sublimated the coatings.
11. [b-dry-grains] The dark irregular grain cores from b-icy-grains without thick pale mantles. IMPORTANT: Names may be needed versus generic dry dust; no liquid puddle or disappearing rocky cores.
12. [b-frosty-dust] Fine pale mantled grains with dark cores barely visible and irregular soft frost edges. IMPORTANT: Fine dust, not icy pebbles or a gas mist; representative magnification is symbolic.

Compare fine angular dry grains, porous aggregates and compact pebbles through real structure; a color swap is insufficient.
Keep the same underlying rocky grain vocabulary in icy, shattered-icy and dry states; ice appears as irregular frost mantles, not gems or droplets.
Rebuilt clumps are new aggregates from fragments, never the exact old clump resurrected. Preserve the distinction between fragmentation and loss of an ice coating.
Grain scale is a representative enlargement within the existing young disk; never draw planets as grains. Relative speed requires ordinary names/context, not new arrows, flame trails or process tokens.
